Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
902 PM EDT Tue Oct 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 224 PM EDT Tuesday...

Have increased the winds in the wider valleys of the region late 
Thursday and Friday ahead and associated with a cold frontal passage.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 224 PM EDT Tuesday...

1. Cold winter like temperatures tonight will be followed by 
gradual warming towards the late week.

2. A cold front late Thursday into Friday will bring chances 
for light rain showers in addition to breezy to gusty winds.

3. Dry weather this weekend, shower chances return next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 224 PM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure centered over the Southeast will continue 
to drive clear skies and cold northwest air into the region through 
tonight. With clear skies remaining into tonight, strong radiational 
cooling will take place with many locations seeing the coldest air 
of the season, with near record cold across portions of Vermont. 
Temperatures will fall to the low 20s for most of the region, 
outside of the higher terrain where a steep inversion will keep lows 
in the upper 20s to near 30. Near record cold at our climate sites 
including Montpelier, St. Johnsbury, and Plattsburgh will be 
possible tonight. A few high clouds late tonight look to limit the 
prime radiational cooling time tonight across much of northern New 
York, otherwise a few records there might also be in jeopardy.

Temperatures will gradually warm and trend to normal as high 
pressure shifts east offshore Wednesday turning winds to the south, 
advecting in warmer air. A glancing mid level trough will bring some 
cloudy skies through the area tomorrow, but surface-mid levels will 
be too dry to see any precipitation. Temperatures will be 5-10 
degrees warmer tomorrow with highs in the low to mid 50s, with our 
cool spots near the International Border and the Northeast Kingdom.

KEY MESSAGE 2: By Thursday, southwest strong waa ushered in by a 45-55 
knot 850 LLJ will warm temperatures steeply well into the 60s. Highs 
in the mid to upper 60s will be possible with areas in the St. 
Lawrence Valley nearing even 70. The warm temperatures will come at 
a price though, as southwest winds will increase to 20-30 MPH, 
particularly in the St. Lawrence and Champlain Valleys. Model 
soundings continue to trend up with top of the mixed layer in the 
recent model suite averaging around 35 MPH. Mixing of these stronger 
winds will be complex as the timing of the precipitation associated 
with the cold front will be entering the region around the time of 
peak mixing, which could temper gusts slightly lower. Regardless, 
Thursday afternoon in the St. Lawrence Valley and near Lake 
Champlain will be gusty. Precipitation will generally be scattered 
with the front due to lingering dry air at the surface, though 
moisture advection with this system will be better than our system 
Monday. A few hundreths up to a tenth of an inch or rainfall is 
expected, focused in the St. Lawrence Valley, Adirondacks, and 
northern Greens. A few showers will linger into Friday along the 
northern mountains, but we will begin to trend drier by Friday 
afternoon. Winds will turn to the west northwest behind the front 
which will bring drier and cooler air by Friday afternoon. Lapse 
rates will steepen Friday afternoon as we dry out with good vertical 
mixing across our northern wider valleys. Winds will increase with 
better chances for seeing some stronger winds up to 30 MPH. Have 
trended winds up as confidence grows for these stronger channeled 
winds Friday afternoon.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Surface high pressure builds over our region for the 
weekend bringing dry weather and temperatures slightly warmer than 
seasonal normals for daytime highs, and cooler than normal overnight 
minimum temperatures. Sunday night into early next week high 
pressure moves east of our region and will have some shower chances 
next week, though lots of uncertainty at this stage.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 00Z Thursday...There will be minimal weather concerns to
aviators for this forecast period with the region under high
pressure. Light winds expected overnight becoming light out of
the south after 12Z with CIGS over 8000ft moving in. There could
be some light virga from this deck at times, but the sub-cloud
layer is dry and any liquid is unlikely to reach the ground.

Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance

Expect generally good air quality in the Champlain Valley, higher elevation locations throughout the remainder of the state, and valley locations without air emission sources.
